title: urnetwork / proxy
description: Authenticated Proxy service deep dive. HTTP and SOCKS traffic is measured at the client-facing relay boundary; WireGuard traffic is measured at the provider-device boundary. Device, peer, session, and cache values are aggregate capacity signals and never carry customer identity. Library event totals and several WireGuard gauges are cumulative for one process generation, so rate panels tolerate restarts. Missing or stale telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: ready instances
panels.description: Instances whose initial peer synchronization completed and which are not draining.

panels.title: drain connections remaining
panels.description: HTTP and SOCKS connections remaining in the active bounded drain. An absent series is not a completed drain.

panels.title: HTTP / SOCKS admissions / s
panels.description: Successful dials and bounded authentication or dial failures. WireGuard has a separate packet admission view.

panels.title: active relay work
panels.description: Successfully dialed upstream sessions plus current in-flight ingress work. These overlap and must not be treated as distinct users.

panels.title: WireGuard sessions
panels.description: Peers whose newest completed handshake is inside the three minute session window, beside every peer registered on the devices. WireGuard has no session teardown: a client with traffic re-handshakes every two minutes and a silent one lets its keys expire at three, so in-session is the honest count of clients actually using the tunnel right now, and the gap to registered peers is clients configured but idle.

panels.title: SOCKS sessions
panels.description: Successfully dialed SOCKS upstream sessions not yet closed, beside the SOCKS ingress work in flight (connections, tunnels and UDP associations as the library reports them). The two overlap and must not be added.

panels.title: proxy devices
panels.description: Embedded provider devices installed on the fleet (live), those with client activity inside the activity window (active), and those pre-warmed at startup from the recent-activity set. Live minus active is idle capacity waiting on its idle timeout; a replacement instance shows pre-warmed rising before active does.

panels.title: new sessions / s
panels.description: Sessions begun per second: WireGuard by a peer's first handshake after having none inside the window, SOCKS by an admitted upstream dial. Reset-aware rates over the selected interval.

panels.title: contract creation storm: calls in flight, outcomes, Redis reservations, pools and host CPU
stuck creations, busiest process
panels.description: CreateContract calls in stage other in the busiest selected proxy process, as each process's two-minute maximum: the count moves in waves as cleanup budgets end together. Stage other counts the time no stage instruments; in the 2026-10-26 storm it held failed calls waiting out their reservation cleanup, about 9k per process. Red from 1,000: the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 26 needs 5 minutes above it. Healthy is at most 30.

panels.title: failure share
panels.description: (canceled + panic) over (contract_reply + canceled + panic) for the CreateContract calls that returned in the last five minutes, as SIGNALS.md section 25.1 defines it: protocol_reject stays out, since it would swamp the share. Shown only with at least 20 such calls/s. Orange from 5% (the WARN, 10 minutes), red from 20% (the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 26, 5 minutes). Healthy is 0-1.3%, 3-5% in the busiest hours. A call counts when it returns, so the share trails the in-flight count.

panels.title: release-pending errors / s
panels.description: Redis release-pending calls that failed, per second over five minutes: reservation cleanup that could not reach Redis. Orange from 10/s: the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26 needs 5 minutes above it. Healthy is at most 0.6/s; 86k/s at the 2026-10-26 storm's peak.

panels.title: Redis pool timeouts / s
panels.description: go-redis pool timeouts of the selected proxy processes per second over five minutes: commands that waited past the pool timeout for a connection. Orange from 10/s (the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26, 5 minutes), red from 1,000/s (the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 3.5b). Sustained timeouts came with reconnect churn on the Redis nodes in the 2026-10-26 storm (HELLO on the Redis cluster dashboard).

panels.title: busiest proxy host CPU
panels.description: Busy share (neither idle nor I/O wait) over five minutes of the busiest host running the selected proxy processes. Orange from 85%: the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26 needs 10 minutes above it. Healthy is 9-51%; the proxy hosts ran 89-96% busy in the 2026-10-26 storm, the last of its signals to rise.

targets.expr: max(1 - sum by (host) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{env="$env",host=~"$host",job="node",mode=~"idle|iowait"}[5m])) / sum by (host) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{env="$env",host=~"$host",job="node"}[5m])) and on (host) count by (host) (go_goroutines{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}))

panels.title: cap refusals / s, busiest process
panels.description: Contract creations the per-process cap (proxy.yml hosted_contract_concurrency, 256 by default) refused at once, per second over five minutes, in the busiest selected process. A process counts only once it has run 30 minutes: a block's own restart brings 12-21 minutes of expected refusals. Orange from 50/s: the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26 needs 10 minutes above it. Refusals mean creations are not returning; the cap protects the process but does not end a storm.

targets.expr: max(sum by (host, block) (rate(urnetwork_hosted_contract_admission_refusals_total{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[5m])) and on (host, block) (time() - max by (host, block) (process_start_time_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > 1800))

panels.title: CreateContract calls in flight by stage
panels.description: Calls now inside each CreateContract stage, summed over the selected processes and stacked, so the top of the stack is every call in flight. Stage other counts the time no stage instruments; reservation cleanup ran there in the 2026-10-26 storm.

panels.title: calls in stage other per process
panels.description: Each process's two-minute maximum of calls in stage other, for the busiest process of each block on each host (a rollout's old and new process show as one line). The line is the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 26: 1,000 for 5 minutes. A process under the per-process cap stays near its capacity (proxy.yml hosted_contract_concurrency, 256 by default); then the cap refusals carry the storm.

targets.expr: max by (host, block) (sum by (host, block, instance) (max_over_time(urnetwork_contract_creation_stage_inflight{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!="",stage="other"}[2m])))

panels.title: CreateContract completions / s by outcome
panels.description: Returned calls per second by outcome. contract_reply hands a contract back (it does not prove delivery); canceled is a call whose caller gave up, counted when the call returns; protocol_reject is a refusal sent to the client, by cause below. In the 2026-10-26 storm contract_reply fell from about 240/s to 25/s while canceled ran 450-1,350/s.

panels.title: failure share (canceled + panic)
panels.description: (canceled + panic) over (contract_reply + canceled + panic), as SIGNALS.md section 25.1 defines it; protocol_reject stays out of both sides. The lines are its WARN at 5% (10 minutes) and the PAGE at 20% (5 minutes, SIGNALS.md section 26), which count only with at least 20 such calls/s. It trails the in-flight count, because a call counts when it returns.

panels.title: contract replies against their 2-hour median
panels.description: Proxy contract_reply per second over five minutes, divided by its median over the two hours that end 10 minutes earlier. Under 0.25 for 10 minutes is the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 26 (shaded). In the 2026-10-26 storm it fell to 0.13 at 14:56Z. The median absorbs a collapse within two hours, so a long storm shows in the stuck calls and the failure share instead; a proxy rollout that resets devices also dips it.

panels.title: contract rejections / s by cause
panels.description: Protocol rejections generated for CreateContract, by cause. deadline is a creation that ran out of time inside the server: 0-0.6/s when healthy, about 1.9k/s at the 2026-10-26 storm's peak. insufficient_balance follows a daily pattern and is not by itself a storm signal.

panels.title: cap slots in use against capacity per process
panels.description: Each process's two-minute maximum of contract creation slots in use, for the busiest process of each block on each host (a rollout's old and new process show as one line), against the slots its cap has (dashed, in the tooltip but not the legend). A slot is one control call made only of CreateContract frames, held until the call returns. The cap is proxy.yml hosted_contract_concurrency, 256 by default, read when a process starts; a value that is not a positive integer keeps 256. A line at its capacity refuses creations (cap refusals, beside it); the gap below is the headroom. With the grant probe (2026-10-26 22:06Z) a process held at most 32 creations in flight from its 30th minute on, and came near its cap only in the first 5 minutes after a restart. Processes without the gauges export nothing.

panels.title: cap refusals / s per process, after 30 minutes
panels.description: Contract creations refused at once by each process's cap (proxy.yml hosted_contract_concurrency, 256 by default), for the processes of each block that have run 30 minutes or more: a block's own restart brings 12-21 minutes of expected refusals, which this leaves out. The line is the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26: 50/s for 10 minutes. A refusal costs no credential, database or Redis work. Processes without the cap export nothing.

targets.expr: sum by (host, block) (rate(urnetwork_hosted_contract_admission_refusals_total{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) and on (host, block) (time() - max by (host, block) (process_start_time_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > 1800)

panels.title: Redis reservation results / s
panels.description: Reservation operations per second by operation and result, on a log scale so a few errors per second show beside thousands of routine refusals. Highlighted: error, dropped and expired in red, pending in orange; routine results are gray. release-pending error is reservation cleanup that could not reach Redis (WARN above 10/s for 5 minutes, SIGNALS.md section 26; 86k/s at the 2026-10-26 peak); reserve-pending refused is normal grant selection, and recovery pending is normal background. handoff moved is a token the deferred compensation owner gave up on and passed to the recovery marker, which the next request on the grant releases at once; handoff error left a token to the 10-minute recovery age, handoff skipped kept one that a live attempt of its request might still publish, handoff disabled was held back by the operator switch (redis_contract_compensation.yml), and handoff slow by a timeout in the owner's calls within the last 30 s.

panels.title: reservation compensation results / s
panels.description: How the token release of each failed creation ended, on a log scale: completed, or pending (balances left reserved). Builds with the deferred compensation owner also count deferred (handed to the process-wide owner after the request's own pass, then counted again as completed, pending or expired), dropped (the owner already held 1,024 balances) and expired (the 5 s budget left the owner no retry). The line is the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26: dropped plus expired above 1/s for 10 minutes. When the owner gives up on a pending or expired compensation it passes each token to the recovery marker (handoff on the reservation results panel), unless the operator switch is off or one of its calls timed out in the last 30 s, and the next request on the grant releases it at once; dropped tokens, and any whose handoff failed, stay reserved until a later request on the grant reclaims them after 10 minutes, or their 24-hour lease ends. On the right axis: the most balances one process's owner holds, waiting for a retry or in a pass (it drops new compensations past 1,024), and the most release calls one process's owner has in flight (at most its 4 workers).

matcher.options: calls in flight (most in one process)

targets.legendFormat: calls in flight (most in one process)

panels.title: Redis client pool timeouts and misses / s
panels.description: go-redis pool timeouts (a command waited past the pool timeout for a connection) and misses (no idle connection, so a new one was dialed) of the selected proxy processes. The lines are for timeouts: the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26 at 10/s (5 minutes) and the PAGE of SIGNALS.md section 3.5b at 1,000/s. Misses in the thousands are reconnect churn; the Redis nodes show it as HELLO.

panels.title: proxy host CPU busy
panels.description: Busy share (neither idle nor I/O wait, summed over the CPUs) of each host that runs the selected proxy processes. The line is the WARN of SIGNALS.md section 26: 85% for 10 minutes. Healthy is 9-51%; read it with the stuck calls, since it rose last in the 2026-10-26 storm.

targets.expr: 1 - sum by (host) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{env="$env",host=~"$host",job="node",mode=~"idle|iowait"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{env="$env",host=~"$host",job="node"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (host) count by (host) (go_goroutines{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: goroutines per process
panels.description: Goroutines of the busiest process of each block on each host. Every hosted device runs its own goroutines, so the count follows the device count and does not by itself show a storm (SIGNALS.md section 26, measured and not adopted): about 215k per process in the 2026-10-26 storm, against 241-287k that morning.

panels.title: proxy process CPU by host
panels.description: CPU cores the selected proxy processes use on each host, beside the host's core count. The processes on one host can demand more cores than it has.

targets.expr: count by (host) (node_cpu_seconds_total{env="$env",host=~"$host",job="node",mode="idle"}) and on (host) count by (host) (go_goroutines{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: WireGuard sessions and peers
panels.description: Peers in session against the registered peer table, with sessions started and ended per second. A session ends when a whole window passes with no new handshake or the peer is removed from the device, so an ended rate that tracks the started rate is churn, and a started rate with a flat in-session count is clients that connect and go quiet at once.

panels.title: SOCKS sessions
panels.description: SOCKS upstream sessions open and ingress work in flight, with sessions opened per second and closed per second by terminal outcome. Closes dominated by read or write errors point at the upstream side of the relay, not at SOCKS clients.

panels.title: mean WireGuard and SOCKS session duration
panels.description: Mean duration of the sessions that ended in each interval, as sum over count of the duration summaries (no histogram buckets, so no cardinality cost). A WireGuard duration is first completed handshake to last, which understates a session by up to one rekey interval; a SOCKS duration is dial to close. Nothing renders in an interval with no ended session.

panels.title: proxy devices
panels.description: Installed embedded devices over time: live, active inside the activity window, and pre-warmed. Active is refreshed on the activity flush cadence, so it lags a burst of new clients by up to a minute. Missing or stale telemetry remains no-data rather than zero.

panels.title: admissions by protocol and outcome
panels.description: Finite outcomes are admitted, unauthorized, and dial_failed; no address or credential is retained.

panels.title: session closes by outcome
panels.description: Completed upstream sessions and bounded read/write terminal failures by HTTP or SOCKS.

panels.title: client-boundary relay bytes / s
panels.description: HTTP/SOCKS body and tunnel bytes on the upstream relay connection: client_to_destination is Write; destination_to_client is Read.

panels.title: mean session duration
panels.description: Rate-derived mean completed HTTP/SOCKS upstream-session duration by finite protocol.

panels.title: fresh one-minute maximum session duration
panels.description: Exact process maxima only while their paired close timestamp is within 120 seconds; no closes or stale publication remains no-data.

targets.expr: max by (protocol) (urnetwork_proxy_session_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, protocol) (urnetwork_proxy_session_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_proxy_session_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: bounded HTTP / SOCKS library events / s
panels.description: Fixed library reasons expose dial, framing, relay, body-limit, upgrade, and UDP-association behavior without request or destination labels.

panels.title: HTTP / SOCKS ingress work
panels.description: Current connections, requests, tunnels, or UDP associations reported by each ingress implementation.

panels.title: WireGuard packets / s by direction and outcome
panels.description: Inner packets offered at the aggregate provider-device boundary; delivered and dropped stay distinct.

panels.title: WireGuard bytes / s by direction and outcome
panels.description: Inner-packet bytes at the provider-device boundary; transport framing is excluded.

panels.title: WireGuard queue drops and receiver failures / s
panels.description: Process-generation cumulative gauges sampled from the device. Rates distinguish peer-queue drops, decryption-queue drops, and unexpected receive-routine exits.

panels.title: aggregate devices, peers, prewarm, and lifecycle
panels.description: Fleet capacity and deployment continuity without device or customer labels. lifecycle join must be 1 per serving instance.

panels.title: device memory target, tracked use, and admission budget
panels.description: Aggregate DeviceLocal steady-state target and tracked live use alongside the process admission budget and its fixed per-device reservations. Compare with process RSS for untracked runtime and pool memory.

panels.title: platform transport byte capacity
panels.description: Aggregate private carrier byte budget, acquired bytes, and bytes waiting for H1 admission.

panels.title: platform transport count capacity
panels.description: Aggregate private carrier slots, pending H1 admission, and sampled same-device preemption rates. Sample-time state does not prove the slot state at each preemption, and legitimate handoffs can temporarily exceed steady-state caps. Use the handoff and provider-window panels below to distinguish known unsatisfied demand from handoff or unknown readiness; totals alone do not prove admission failure.

panels.title: WireGuard return backpressure
panels.description: Packets that waited for bounded receive-queue capacity plus mean and p95 wait duration.

panels.title: caller-lock cache occupancy
panels.description: Bounded aggregate cache entries and hard capacity; no address or proxy credential is exported.

panels.title: caller-lock cache activity / s
panels.description: Cache hits, misses, expirations, and hard-bound evictions without caller labels.

panels.title: control and device-RPC HTTP outcomes
panels.description: Bounded configured control routes include status, warmup, and the hosted device RPC lifecycle. Hijacked sessions retain route outcome and duration without path labels.

panels.title: control and device-RPC bytes and inflight
panels.description: HTTP body bytes exclude bytes sent after a WebSocket hijack; in-flight route duration remains the RPC session control. Absence is not interpreted as zero traffic.

panels.title: control and device-RPC mean / fresh max
panels.description: Mean configured-route duration plus the exact process maximum while its paired observation is fresh. A hosted WebSocket's duration covers its served session after hijack.

targets.expr: max by (route) (urnetwork_http_request_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, route) (urnetwork_http_request_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_http_request_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="proxy",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: control-plane database and Redis pressure
panels.description: Initialized PostgreSQL pools and Redis connections used by proxy synchronization, authorization, warmup, and device control.

panels.title: process CPU, memory, goroutines, and file descriptors
panels.description: Proxy process saturation controls by selected deployment block and host.

panels.title: proxy devices live
panels.description: Installed hosted devices by process. Each owns an independent 24 MiB memory target; this is not a process-wide admission ceiling. Compare with host reserve and OOM telemetry when sizing hardware.

panels.title: tracked device memory / target by process
panels.description: Sum of private DeviceLocal tracked usage divided by the sum of their 24 MiB targets. This is not an aggregate admission gate or total process RSS; a low ratio must not be read as host spare capacity.

panels.title: active platform handoff slot allowance
panels.description: Current temporary carrier-count allowance owned by active private-budget H1/H3 handoffs, aggregated per process. This is allowance, not acquired carriers or steady-state spare capacity; compare with the private transport budget and used counts. Missing telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: active platform handoff byte allowance
panels.description: Current temporary byte allowance owned by active private-budget H1/H3 handoffs, aggregated per process. This is allowance, not tracked memory use or steady-state spare capacity; compare with acquired carrier bytes and the private byte budget. Missing telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: slot-full H1 admission context by process
panels.description: Instantaneous counts of DeviceLocals with pending H1 admission at a full carrier-count cap. Handoff state is sampled from the same private budget and includes pending or active handoffs. Handoff + unsatisfied is a subset with a known unsatisfied provider window; no handoff + unsatisfied requires that window without a handoff. Window unknown means readiness is unavailable, not failed or healthy. These counts overlap and are not a partition of the total; do not stack or add them. Samples are aggregated per process without device/customer identifiers; missing telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: hosted registrations and contract creations refused, and invalid performance profiles / s
panels.description: Hosted derived-client registrations and contract creations refused because the owner's concurrent registration or contract creation bound was full, and stored initial performance profiles that connect refuses, read back in auto by this service. A refused creation is asked again on the device's own retry schedule. The API dashboard shows the auth-client refusals.

panels.title: removed-client device closes, subscriptions and read failures / s
panels.description: Hosted devices closed because their client was removed through the api, by what found the removal; subscriptions and resubscriptions to the removed-client key events, each of which checks the installed devices' clients; and removed-flag reads that failed, whose devices wait for the next subscription or their idle timeout (CLIENTCLOSE.md section 5).
